title: partner-saas-marketplace-entry-criteria-and-landing-snippets
body:
Purpose
This is a compact, practical playbook for getting a partner SaaS listing live across cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP). Focus is on the minimal acceptance criteria, buyer-facing landing tile copy for three key personas, and a short preflight checklist that engineering, legal and partner success can run in ~48 hours.

Scope and audience
- Audience: Partner PM, Partner Engineer, GTM launch PM, and Partner Success.
- Outcome: partner receives a prescriptive list of required assets + 3 tile copy variants they can pick and tweak.

Quick summary (one-liner)
- What we need from partner: 5 assets (tile image, 1-paragraph description, 3 persona snippets, SKU & trial config, security declarations).
- We will validate via: automated acceptance tests (billing + SSO), manual UX sanity pass, and legal checklist.
- Typical turnaround: 1–2 weeks with complete assets; 48–72 hours with self-hosted/managed partners who fill the quick-form.

Minimal entry criteria (must-have)
1) Tile assets
   - High-resolution tile image (1200x628 px recommended, PNG or JPG).
   - 1 x 64x64 icon (square, PNG).
2) Short copy
   - One-line subtitle (<= 75 chars).
   - One-paragraph body (<= 280 chars) describing product and primary benefit.
   - 3 persona-targeted blurbs (developer, platform engineer, security/compliance buyer).
3) Trial & SKU configuration
   - SKU code (alphanumeric) and pricing tier mapping.
   - Trial plan: duration (14/30 days), provisioning mechanism (self-serve activation link, trial entitlements API, or marketplace trial).
   - Terms link (hosted URL to partner T&Cs).
4) Security & compliance basics
   - Data processing location (regions) and KMS usage summary (yes/no).
   - SOC2 or ISO status (attach certificate or link).
   - Contact for security questions (email).
5) Technical acceptance
   - Integration test endpoint and sample API key (sandbox).
   - Healthcheck endpoint with 200 response and example payloads.
   - Latency SLO guidance (p95 < X ms) and average token cost estimate (if applicable).
6) Legal & billing
   - Registered company name and billing contact.
   - Tax and invoicing details for the selected marketplace (partner to confirm).

Persona tile copy snippets (pick one per persona, tweak tone)
1) Developer (aim: fast trial + easy SDKs):
   - Title: "Low-latency LLM inference, ready for devs"
   - Subtitle: "Ship features faster with plug-and-play SDKs"
   - Body (short): "Integrate high-throughput LLM endpoints with SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. Start with a free 14-day trial and example prompts for common UX patterns."
2) Platform engineer (aim: predictable ops & cost):
   - Title: "Predictable inference at scale"
   - Subtitle: "Dedicated pools, cost controls, and autoscale"
   - Body (short): "Reserve GPUs for consistent latency, configure batching and caching policies, and get per-token cost breakdowns at the route level. Trial includes a staging pool for load testing."
3) Security/compliance buyer (aim: data control & governance):
   - Title: "Private deployments and enterprise controls"
   - Subtitle: "Bring your VPC, KMS, and audit logs"
   - Body (short): "Private deployment options with KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 support. Request a trial to validate network and key management flows."

UX landing guidance (quick rules)
- Primary CTA: "Start free trial" (opens activation modal or marketplace trial flow).
- Secondary CTA: "Request demo" (links to calendar + optional enterprise questionnaire).
- Top three bullets visible above the fold: 1) what you get in trial, 2) key differentiator (e.g., "dedicated pools"), 3) security callout.
- Avoid dense technical paragraphs on the tile; put details in the expanded detail page.

Preflight acceptance checklist (fast 48–72h run)
Ownership: partner engineers + Redwood partner PM
- [ ] Tile image and icon uploaded and visually validated (UI sanity)
- [ ] One-line subtitle and paragraph approved by partner marketing
- [ ] Persona snippets provided and mapped to buyer segments
- [ ] SKU and trial configuration entered in partner portal
- [ ] Sandbox API key issued and smoke-tested (auth + simple inference call)
- [ ] Healthcheck endpoint returns 200 and sample response matches contract
- [ ] Security contact listed and SOC2/ISO link provided
- [ ] Billing & tax info captured for the marketplace SKU
- [ ] Legal terms link available and accessible
- [ ] Marketplace-specific fields filled (e.g., product category, tags)

Technical smoke tests (engineering)
- Auth smoke: exchange partner sandbox key -> 200 on /v1/infer with sample payload
- Health smoke: GET /health -> 200 and {"status":"ok"} (or partner-defined)
- Billing signal: make a test purchase flow (or sim) and confirm webhook delivered to provided URL
- Latency check: run 10 calls at the expected trial concurrency and report p50/p95

Operational play: rollout & fallback
- Default rollout: publish in one marketplace region (US) + internal validation window 48h.
- Canary: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 100% (manual checks at each step).
- Fallback: if health checks fail, routing policy will revert to Redwood-hosted stable model (partner tile shows limited availability message).

Legal & compliance short notes
- For marketplace listing we need either a hosted terms URL or a short excerpt to include in the tile detail. If the partner requires custom EULA handling, mark as enterprise (not eligible for self-serve listing).
- If partner stores customer data, they must provide region-level controls and a KMS binding plan for Private deployments; include KMS contact for the partner.

Examples of micro-variants to A/B test on tile (copy + CTA)
- Variant A (developer-first): Emphasize SDKs + quick start
- Variant B (ops-first): Emphasize dedicated capacity + cost controls
- Variant C (enterprise): Emphasize compliance + private deployment
Run each variant for 72h on 30% of impressions during the launch week. Measure trial signups and first-week activation rate.

Known marketplace quirks (short list)
- AWS: tile images can be auto-resized; ensure important text sits inside safe area
- Azure: SKU mappings require explicit metering dimensions; if using usage-based billing, include clear unit description
- GCP: trial flows sometimes need partner-provided provisioning hooks for entitlements; clarify API contract early

Recommended minimal timeline
- Day 0–2: partner submits assets and trial config + security artifacts
- Day 3–5: engineering smoke tests + billing test + UX pass
- Day 6–8: legal review and final marketplace submission
- Day 9–14: marketplace approval windows (varies by marketplace)

Contacts and escalation
- Partner PM (Redwood): Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.ai)
- Partner Engineer (Redwood): Aditi Menon (aditi@redwood.ai)
- Marketplace ops (Redwood): Carlos Reyes (carlos@redwood.ai)
- Security reviewer: Ethan Park (ethan@redwood.ai)

Open questions to close with partner
- Do you require custom trial entitlements beyond a 14-day window?
- Are there regional data residency constraints important for listing copy?
- Do you want us to run initial A/B variants or pass that to your growth team?

Notes to the reviewer
- This doc is intentionally compact — use the checklist as the source-of-truth during intake calls.
- We should create a partner intake form in the portal that maps to this checklist (fields + file uploads) to reduce back-and-forth.

Revision history
- 2024-11-10: initial draft (Maya)
- 2024-11-14: added persona snippets and smoke tests (Aditi)
- 2024-11-18: clarified legal notes and timeline (Carlos)

End of doc
